signals.title: AUD/USD — G10 Bilateral Theme + Commodity Support
signals.text: AUD/USD trades at 0.7031, holding above its SMA20 at 0.6979 while facing dynamic overhead resistance near the SMA50/200 area around 0.7047–0.7080. The G10 scorecard shows AUD outperforming all peers with a 1W average gain of +1.449% across 4 pairs, contrasted against USD as the G10 laggard at -0.833% across 9 pairs, driving a 2.282% bilateral spread. A 60bp rate differential favors AUD with RBA at 4.60% (hiking bias) vs Fed at 4.00% (hiking stance), creating structural carry support. CFTC Leveraged Funds net long sits at +44,978 contracts (pctl 54, z +0.38), indicating institutional positioning is balanced rather than stretched. Divergence between spot outperformance and short-term US real yield momentum suggests near-term upside may face friction near 0.7080. Trade bias: Long AUD/USD; monetary policy carry advantage and peer strength offset overhead moving average resistance. Catalyst: RBA policy meeting 3 Nov — hold expected at 4.60%. Risk: Sustained daily close below SMA20 at 0.6979 invalidates the weekly outperformance theme.

signals.title: USD/JPY — Carry Support vs Options Risk Reversal Skew
signals.text: USD/JPY trades at 158.13, consolidating above its SMA20 at 158.01 and SMA50 at 157.68 within a tight 20-session range. The 275bp policy rate differential (Fed 4.00% vs BoJ 1.25%) and +264bp SOFR-TONA OIS carry spread sustain fundamental structural support for the pair. However, options pricing reveals persistent downside hedging demand, with 25d Risk Reversals printing at -1.86, a strong put skew reflecting elevated demand for JPY call protection. COT positioning shows Leveraged Funds net short JPY at -37,820 contracts (pctl 88, z +1.08), showing spec positioning is elevated within its trailing 52-week window. The combination of carry demand against downside options skew signals late-range consolidation with asymmetric unwind risk if key support breaks. Trade bias: Neutral/long USD/JPY; elevated carry return competes against institutional options hedging. Catalyst: BoJ rate decision 30 Oct — hold expected at 1.25%. Risk: Break below SMA50 at 157.68 triggers unwinds of Leveraged Fund JPY shorts.

signals.title: EUR/USD — Positioning Squeeze + Volatility Risk Premium
signals.text: EUR/USD trades at 1.1236, holding below its SMA20 (1.1263), SMA50 (1.1459), and SMA200 (1.1586) in a broader counter-trend structure. Saxo FX Options show 1M ATM IV at 6.6% versus HV30 at 4.2%, creating a +2.5% Volatility Risk Premium (VRP) that signals elevated institutional hedging demand relative to realized movement. CFTC data indicates Leveraged Funds are heavily short EUR at -92,833 contracts, sitting at the 4th percentile of its 52-week range (z -1.78), creating an extreme positioning imbalance. Meanwhile, OIS carry favors USD via a +143bp SOFR-€STR spread (Fed 4.00% vs ECB 2.65%), providing structural carry headwinds to EUR recoveries. The combination of extreme spec shorts and elevated option implied volatility creates asymmetric short-squeeze potential on any hawkish ECB repricing. Trade bias: Neutral/short EUR/USD; extreme spec short positioning creates short-squeeze risk despite negative carry spread. Catalyst: ECB policy meeting 29 Oct — hold expected at 2.65%. Risk: Daily close above SMA20 at 1.1263 forces capitulation covering among spec shorts.

signals.title: NZD/USD — Upcoming Inflation Catalyst vs Data Surprises
signals.text: NZD/USD trades at 0.5704, holding above its SMA20 at 0.5632 while remaining capped below the SMA50 at 0.5769 following a recovery from mid-October lows. RBNZ policy sits at 2.75% (hiking stance) against the Fed at 4.00%, creating a +125bp USD carry advantage, though OIS markets price active expectations for further RBNZ tightening. New Zealand's Economic Surprise Index sits at -7.4, reflecting recent domestic data disappointments that contrast with Leveraged Fund net short positioning of -11,802 contracts (pctl 58). With Q3 CPI forecast at 1.4% q/q (5.1% y/y) releasing imminently at 21:45 UTC, short-term repricing risk is elevated ahead of the 28 Oct RBNZ decision. An upside inflation print threatens to trigger covering in spec shorts toward the SMA50 level. Trade bias: Long NZD/USD; technical recovery above SMA20 aligned with hawkish policy catalyst setup. Catalyst: NZ Q3 CPI release at 21:45 UTC — forecast 1.4% q/q. Risk: CPI miss below 1.2% q/q confirms negative ESI trajectory and reopens downside toward 0.5632.

signals.title: USD/NOK — Retail Positioning Divergence + High Real Yield
signals.text: USD/NOK trades at 9.4000, holding below its SMA20 (9.527), SMA50 (9.419), and SMA200 (9.529) in an established technical downtrend. Retail sentiment data retail sentiment shows 100% of retail accounts net long USD/NOK, establishing an extreme one-sided retail consensus that acts as a strong contrarian indicator favoring further downside. Norges Bank policy rate at 4.50% (hiking stance) versus Fed at 4.00% provides a +50bp nominal rate advantage for NOK, while Norway's positive real policy rate (+1.82%) and strong ESI (+17.2) underscore robust fundamental backing. BEER model fair value measures USD/NOK as cheap at z = -1.65σ (spot 9.4000 vs fair value 9.5191), suggesting long-term mean reversion potential that conflicts with short-term retail positioning flows. The extreme retail long stack leaves the pair vulnerable to continued downside pressure as retail stops get cleared. Trade bias: Bearish USD/NOK; 100% retail long extreme provides contrarian short signal backed by positive NOK real yield. Catalyst: Norges Bank policy decision 5 Nov — hold expected at 4.50%. Risk: Sharp rebound in WTI crude oil prices forcing momentum unwinds across Scandinavia.
